question: P and S are two points lying on the same side of a line segment QR such that ∠PQS = 35°, ∠SQR = 50°, ∠SRP = 35° and ∠PRQ = 50°. Then,

options.text: Δ SRQ ~ Δ PQR by AA
Δ PSR ~ Δ SPR by SSS
Δ QPR ≅ Δ RSP by SSS
Δ PRQ ≅ Δ SRP by AA

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the total angles at the base for both triangles by adding the given adjacent angles.

Total angle ∠PQR = ∠PQS + ∠SQR = 35° + 50° = 85°.

Total angle ∠SRQ = ∠SRP + ∠PRQ = 35° + 50° = 85°.

In ΔSRQ and ΔPQR, we clearly see that ∠SRQ = ∠PQR = 85° and ∠SQR = ∠PRQ = 50°.

Since two corresponding angles are exactly equal, the two triangles are similar by the AA (Angle-Angle) similarity criterion.

**∴ The correct answer is Δ SRQ ~ Δ PQR by AA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ∠PQS = 35°, ∠SQR = 50°

⇒ ∠SRP = 35°, ∠PRQ = 50°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total angle at Q for ΔPQR = ∠PQS + ∠SQR = 35° + 50° = 85°

⇒ Total angle at R for ΔSRQ = ∠SRP + ∠PRQ = 35° + 50° = 85°

⇒ In ΔPQR:

⇒ ∠PQR = 85°, and ∠PRQ = 50°

⇒ ∠QPR = 180° − (85° + 50°) = 45°

⇒ In ΔSRQ:

⇒ ∠SRQ = 85°, and ∠SQR = 50°

⇒ ∠QSR = 180° − (85° + 50°) = 45°

⇒ Comparing corresponding angles of ΔSRQ and ΔPQR:

⇒ ∠S = ∠P = 45°

⇒ ∠R = ∠Q = 85°

⇒ ∠Q = ∠R = 50°

⇒ Since all corresponding angles are equal, the two triangles are similar.

⇒ Matching the corresponding vertices gives us S → P, R → Q, and Q → R.

**∴ The correct answer is Δ SRQ ~ Δ PQR by AA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AA (Angle-Angle) Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles of another triangle, then the third angles are also equal, making the two triangles similar.

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence Rule

If all three corresponding sides of two triangles are equal in length, then the two triangles are strictly congruent to each other.

Angle Sum Property of Triangle

The sum of all three interior angles of a triangle is always equal to 180°. This rule is used universally to find missing internal angles.
